question.text: When selecting a jurisdiction for an offshore feeder fund, the requirement to choose an 'equivalent jurisdiction' under anti-money-laundering rules refers to a jurisdiction that:

answer.text: Has the lowest corporate tax rate globally
Complies with Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards on AML and Combating Financing of Terrorism (CFT)
Permits bearer shares and anonymous ownership
Is listed as a tax haven by the OECD

explanation.text: The Logic: Each country publishes a list of 'equivalent jurisdictions' that follow FATF AML/CFT standards. An offshore feeder must be in such a jurisdiction — else onshore AIF and Indian banks will have challenges accepting inflows. FATF is the inter-governmental body setting global AML/CFT standards. The Trap: Option A confuses AML with tax optimisation. Options C and D are OPPOSITE of compliant — bearer shares / tax-haven status raise AML red flags, not green lights. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV (AML) covers FATF rigorously. XIX-A/B/C/D/E all touch FATF equivalence in structuring. Manager's Pro-Tip: Check RBI/SEBI circulars for the current list of 'non-compliant' FATF jurisdictions before picking a feeder location — inflows from those jurisdictions face enhanced due diligence and operational friction.
